text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- First step after 23 years on the issue of the missing persons. Glafcos Clerides and Rauf Denktash agree to procedures on opening graves and returning the remains of relatives. An agreement is also expected between the two sides on the issue of free movement.
- Cabinet appoints new directors to the boards of semi-government organisations.
- Pavlos Georgiou gets 15 months in prison for negligently infecting British lover Janette Pink with the HIV virus which causes AIDS.
- Most of the persons appointed to the boards of semi-government organisations are members of right-wing Disy party or centre-right Diko.
- Clerides and Denktash agree finally on opening graves of suspected missing persons. The deal, if implemented, is the most significant breakthrough in the issue of missing persons since 1974.
- Auditor general's report gives a sorry state of affairs in cooperative credit societies, listing accumulation of bad debts and mismanagement as rife.
- Opening of graves of missing persons is expected to start before the end of 1997.
- Parliament abolishes law on free post-graduate education at Cyprus university.
